name: two bistable coordinates with an antiferromagnetic coupling
question: Under a slow uniform drive, which states do two coupled bistable coordinates reach, does every excursion return to its turning point, and which hysterons do they reduce to?
assumptions: each coordinate relaxes in its own quartic potential x - x^3, much faster than the drive changes
a linear antiferromagnetic coupling J < 0 and the same drive H on both coordinates
fields +a and -a of opposite sign separate the thresholds of the two elements; with a = 0 the elements are identical and their switching is a choice that noise makes
no noise: the quasi-static dynamics of the equations

provenance.source: the double-well (quartic) element of the random-field Ising model in its soft-spin form: J. P. Sethna et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 70, 3347 (1993); K. Dahmen and J. P. Sethna, Phys. Rev. B 53, 14872 (1996)
